transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... I hope I'm explaining this right, so please just stop me if I'm not giving you what you need. But, I guess what made me come in is that, for the past year or so... I've been having this little issue. It's probably nothing major, honestly, just me being a bit scattered, you know? But the smallest thing will just pull me completely off what I'm doing before I can stop it. 

Like... a phone buzz, or somebody walking past my office door, or even just a random thought about my in-laws popping into my head. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, because I run a company and I feel like I should be able to just put my head down and work, right? But it just pulls my attention right away. 

I manage okay, really, but I just wanted to get your thoughts on it. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you usually help people with?
Looking back, were you already this easily distracted as a child?

Um, yeah, I guess looking back... it was kind of like that when I was a kid, too. I mean, I think I was just a really energetic kid, honestly. Nothing terrible! 

But, well, I do remember my teachers were always moving my seat around. I guess I talked a bit too much for their liking. And I'd, um... I'd get up without asking sometimes, or I'd just kind of blurt things out before they even finished asking a question. I was just really eager to participate, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid or a troublemaker. I really wasn't trying to be, I just had a lot of energy. 

Is that... does that help answer your question? I can try to think of something else if that's not what you meant.
Have you ever had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy the next day?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely have nights where I don't sleep great—who doesn't, right, especially running a business? But I wouldn't say I ever feel, like, super energized after not sleeping. If I miss sleep, I'm usually pretty tired the next day, just like anyone else would be. 

I don't think I've ever had a time where I just didn't need sleep at all. Is that... is that something I should be watching out for? I hope it's okay that I haven't experienced that.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to solve?

Um, no, not really. I mean, obviously, with the business, there are always actual fires to put out, so I do think about work a lot. But I wouldn't say I just sit around worrying when there's nothing wrong, you know? 

If there's a real problem in front of me, I just try to handle it. But if everything's fine... I don't really stress over things that aren't there. I try to keep a pretty positive mindset, honestly. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, I'm not trying to sound like I don't care about things, I just... I don't really get anxious out of nowhere. Is that what you were asking, or did I completely misunderstand?
Have you noticed your attention has gotten worse recently compared with how it used to be for most of your adult life?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say it's gotten *worse* in a bad way, exactly. I've always been a bit, you know, on the go. But... yeah, I suppose it has been a little harder to keep a handle on things recently. 

It's been maybe... about a year and two months? Give or take. But it's just because we've had some family stuff going on. There's been this whole conflict with my in-laws, and it's just kind of taken over a lot of our family life, so my mind has been a bit pulled in different directions. Anyone would be a little distracted by that, right? 

I really try not to let it affect my work or anything, I promise. It's just a lot to juggle. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
